## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components in an AoS layout can approach the streaming ceiling on low-death-rate workloads, with the death verdict kept in registers.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/p AoS layout gives sequential stride-68 access the prefetcher tracks. Loop 1 touches 32 of 68 B/p (47% hot — age+pos+seed+vel); loop 2 touches 28 of 68 B/p (41% hot — color+pos); the rest is dead weight in line fills — at 68 B/p each particle spans just over one 64 B cacheline. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers, but loop 1's branchy respawn and loop 2's byte-granular scatter share the same stream. Working set spills L1d at N≈481, L2 at N≈7710, L3 at N≈246723.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is flat across L1d through L3: 7.4 at N=320, 7.6 at N=7700 (L2), then drops to 6.8 at N=99000–160000 (L3) — larger N amortizes call overhead while L3 avoids DRAM. The L1d→L2 and L2→L3 transitions are invisible. The only knee is L3→DRAM at N=250000: 6.8→8.4, settling at ~10.5 by N=370000. The dense grid resolves this knee. At higher q the same shape holds but shifted up; the DRAM knee shrinks proportionally because respawn overhead dominates memory latency.

## Bandwidth
Memory floor is 5.359 ns/p; best achieved is 6.8 ns/p (q=0.01, L3) — 1.27× the floor, 79% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. In DRAM, drops to 6.4 GB/s (51%). Bandwidth-bound at q=0.01 (backend_stall 60–74%), shifting branch-bound at higher q: at q=0.5, branch_flush reaches 12.7% and BW falls to 4.0 GB/s (31%). Versus baseline: 3.0× faster at q=0.01 (0.33×), 2.0× at q=0.5 (0.50×) — branchy respawn is the equalizer. Winner at every point (1.0×).

## Assembly
Loop 1 has partial auto-vectorization: `vmovups` loads the 16 B pos block, `vmulps`/`vaddps` do vector FP, `vbroadcastss`/`vinsertps`/`vshufps` handle shuffles — but 14 cond-branches and 6 scalar FP ops (including `vucomiss` for the death test) break the chain. Respawn issues a `call` plus inline xorshift (`rorx`, `shl`, `xor`, `lzcnt`). Loop 2 is select-based (`cmovb` ×12) with byte-granular scatter (×18 `movzx`/`add`/`mov BYTE PTR`) and `vpaddusb` for saturated byte adds. Stride-68 `vmovups` explains the high L3 bandwidth; the byte-granular stores cap it below ceiling.

## Verdict
Partially holds — at q=0.01 the algo sustains 10.0 GB/s (79% of ceiling, 1.27× the floor), 3.0× faster than naive, winning every point. But it never reaches the ceiling: the 47% hot fraction wastes bandwidth on dead bytes, and byte-granular scatter plus branchy respawn (branch_flush 12.7% at q=0.5, BW at 31% of ceiling) prevent full streaming. The hypothesis holds for low death rates in cache-resident regimes; it breaks at q≥0.25 where branch overhead dominates.
